stem.text: An open-top baking pan is made from a rectangular sheet of steel 45 decimeters by 72 decimeters by cutting a square of side x from each corner and folding up the sides. Find the largest possible volume of the baking pan, in cubic decimeters.

worked_solution.text: The baking pan has height x and a base \( 45 - 2 x \) by \( 72 - 2 x \), so its volume is \( V(x) = x\left(45 - 2 x\right)\left(72 - 2 x\right) \).
The cut must be positive and less than half the sheet, so the domain is \( 0 < x < \frac{45}{2} \).
\( V'(x) = 12 \left(x - 30\right) \left(x - 9\right) \), which is zero at \( x = 9 \) and \( x = 30 \); only \( x = 9 \) lies strictly inside the sheet.
\( V'(x) \) is positive for \( 0 < x < 9 \) and negative for \( 9 < x < \frac{45}{2} \), and this is the only critical point in the domain, so V has its absolute maximum there.
worked_solution.rule_named: first derivative test for an absolute extremum

worked_solution.text: The largest volume is \( V(9) = 9\left(27\right)\left(54\right) = 13122 \) cubic decimeters.

options.derivation: the shorter side of the base at the optimum reported instead of the volume
the side of the cut square, where the maximum occurs, reported instead of the volume
the longer side of the base at the optimum reported instead of the volume
